Rashi on Ketubot 3a:12:1.english: When courts were in regular session every day - That is to say, the fixed status of all days was equal.

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:14:1.english: And don't we require "they were zealous" - That he exert himself with the feast for three days.

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:14:2.hebrew: דטריח ליה - אם טרח לפני השבת ותיקן צורכי סעודה, כונסה באחד בשבת או בשני בשבת:
Rashi on Ketubot 3a:14:2.english: Where he exerted himself - If he exerted himself before Shabbat and prepared the needs of the feast, he may marry her on Sunday or on Monday.

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:1:1.english: Sometimes he was not detained by an accident - And it is a [valid] get.

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:1:2.hebrew: וסברה - דלמא אניס ואינו גט, ותדאג להינשא:
Rashi on Ketubot 3a:1:2.english: And she thinks - Perhaps he was unavoidably detained and it is not a bill of divorce, and she will be afraid to remarry.

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:1:3.hebrew: ומינסבא - וכשיבא ויאמר: ״נאנסתי״, נמצא גט בטל, ובניה מן האחרון ממזרים. לפיכך אמרו: יהא גט:
Rashi on Ketubot 3a:1:3.english: And she remarries - And when he comes and says, "I was detained by an unavoidable accident," the bill of divorce turns out to be void, and her children from the latter [husband] are mamzerim. Therefore, [the Sages] said: It shall be a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:2:1.hebrew: דמדאורייתא לא הוי גיטא - שמצינו טענת אונס מן התורה, שנאמר (דברים כ״ב:כ״ו) ולנערה לא תעשה דבר:
Rashi on Ketubot 3a:2:1.english: That by Torah law it is not a bill of divorce - For we find a claim of circumstances beyond one's control in the Torah, as it is said (Deuteronomy 22:26): "And to the maiden you shall do nothing."

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:3:1.hebrew: כל המקדש - כל המקדש אשה על דעת שהנהיגו חכמי ישראל בישראל הוא מקדשה, שיהיו קיימין קידושין לפי דברי חכמים, ויהיו בטילים לפי דברי חכמים על ידי גיטין שהכשירו חכמים:
Rashi on Ketubot 3a:3:1.english: Whoever betroths - Whoever betroths a woman betroths her with the understanding that the Sages of Israel instituted in Israel: that the betrothal will remain valid according to the words of the Sages, and will become void according to the words of the Sages through bills of divorce that the Sages validated.

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:3:2.english: And the Sages nullified the betrothal - When such a bill of divorce comes after them [the betrothal].

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:4:1.hebrew: תינח - למימר אפקעתא כדקדיש בכספא, דנימא גט זה עוקר הקידושין ועושה מעות מתנה מעיקרן:
Rashi on Ketubot 3a:4:1.english: This works out well - To say [that there is] an expropriation when he betrothed [her] with money, for we can say that this bill of divorce uproots the betrothal and renders the money a gift from the outset.

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:4:3.hebrew: שויוה רבנן לבעילתו - למפרע, על ידי גט שהוא מדבריהם, בעילת זנות, ויש בהן כח לעשות כן, שהרי הוא תלה בהן. שמעתי כל רבותי מפרשים: דקדיש בכספא — דקידושי דרבנן נינהו, ואי אפשר לומר כן: חדא, דגזירה שוה היא: קיחה קיחה משדה עפרון (קידושין דף ב.), וכל הלמד מגזירה שוה כמו שכתוב מפורש הוא לכל דבר. ועוד, אי דרבנן נינהו, היאך סוקלין על ידו, ומביאין חולין לעזרה על שגגתן?! וסוף סוף, כי קא משנינן שויוה רבנן לבעילתו בעילת זנות, על כרחך צריך אתה לפרש כמו שפירשתי: שהקידושין נעקרין מעיקרן, ולא מכאן ולהבא. והמפרש לומר שויוה רבנן לכל מקדשי בביאה בעילת זנות — טעות גמור הוא, ובא להתיר אשת איש המתקדשת בביאה בלא גט מן הטעם הזה, ולא מצינו זאת בהתלמוד:
Rashi on Ketubot 3a:4:3.english: The Sages rendered his intercourse - Retroactively, by means of a bill of divorce that is [valid] by their Rabbinic authority, [to be] an act of fornication. And they have the power to do so, for he made [his betrothal] dependent upon them. I heard all my teachers explain that [the Gemara states,] "he betrothed with money," [because] betrothal with money is Rabbinic; but it is impossible to say so: First, because it is [derived from] a verbal analogy [gezeira shava]: "taking" [kikha], "taking" [kikha] from the field of Ephron (Kiddushin 2a); and anything derived from a verbal analogy is like that which is explicitly written [in the Torah] for all matters. And furthermore, if it were Rabbinic, how could [one] be stoned on its account, and [how could one] bring non-sacred [animals into] the Temple courtyard for their unwitting transgression?! And ultimately, when we answer, "The Sages rendered his intercourse an act of fornication," perforce you must explain as I explained: that the betrothal is uprooted from its inception, and not [merely] from now onward. And one who explains [this] to mean, "The Sages rendered [the intercourse of] all who betroth through intercourse an act of fornication" — this is a complete error, and leads to permitting a married woman who was betrothed through intercourse [to remarry] without a bill of divorce on this account; and we do not find this in the Talmud.

Rashi on Ketubot 3a:5:1.hebrew: וכן לענין גיטין - אלפיכך קאי, דטענינן טענת אונס בתנאי הגט להפקיעו:
Rashi on Ketubot 3a:5:1.english: And so too with regard to bills of divorce - [This] refers to "Therefore" [above (page 2a)] — that we advance a claim of unavoidable circumstances regarding the condition of the bill of divorce, to void it.

Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:12:1.hebrew: שבתי דינין קבועים בכל יום - וא"ת: וכי תיקן עזרא שלא יהו בתי דינין קבועים בכל יום, אלא בב' ובה' בלבד? ועוד קשה, דאמרינן בשבת (ד' קכט: ושם): מי שיש לו זכות אבות יקיז בב' ובה' — וכי קודם תקנת עזרא לא היו מקיזין כל עיקר? ואומר ר"ת, דקודם תקנת עזרא לא היו קבועים בכל יום, אלא כשהיו צריכין לשום דין היו יושבין בכל יום ויום; ועזרא תיקן שיהיו קבועין בב' ובה', וכל הרוצה לדון יבא וידון; והיו יכולין להקיז בכל יום קודם תקנת עזרא, כיון שלא היו קבועים. ור"י תירץ, שלא היו קבועים תחלה אלא בעיר אחת, ועזרא תיקן בכל עיר ועיר בב' ובה':
Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:12:1.english: That courts were fixed every day - And if you say: Did Ezra institute that courts should not be fixed every day, but rather only on Mondays and Thursdays? Furthermore, it is difficult, as we say in Shabbat (129b, and there): "One who has ancestral merit may let blood on Mondays and Thursdays" — did they then not let blood at all prior to Ezra's ordinance? And Rabbeinu Tam says that prior to Ezra's ordinance, [courts] were not fixed [in regular session] every day; rather, whenever they were needed for any legal case, they would sit on any given day. And Ezra instituted that they should be fixed on Mondays and Thursdays, and whoever wishes to litigate may come and litigate. And they were able to let blood on any day prior to Ezra's ordinance, since [the courts] were not fixed [in regular session]. And the Ri answered that initially they were fixed only in one city, and Ezra instituted [that they be fixed] in each and every city on Mondays and Thursdays.

Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:12:2.hebrew: אשה נשאת בכל יום - קשה לרשב"א: אמאי נשאת בכל יום? תהא כאלמנה, ותינשא בה' ותיבעל בששי, לפי שנאמר בו ברכה לאדם. וי"ל, דמשום ברכה לא היו קובעים יום, כדפרישית לעיל. ובאלמנה נמי, לא קבעו שתיבעל בששי משום ברכה גרידא, אלא משום שקדו, שיהא שמח עמה ג' ימים, כדאמר לקמן (כתובות דף ה.). ובתולה, דלא שייך ההוא טעמא, דליכא למימר משכים לאומנתו והולך לו, לפי שיש בה שבעת ימי המשתה; הלכך, משום ברכה גרידא לא היו קובעים יום:
Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:12:2.english: A woman is married on any day - The Rashba asks: Why is she married on any day? Let her be like a widow, and be married on Thursday and consummate [the marriage] on Friday, since blessing was said on it for mankind! And one can say that because of blessing [alone] they would not establish a [fixed] day, as I explained above. And regarding a widow as well, they did not establish that she should consummate [the marriage] on Friday because of blessing alone, but rather because [the Sages] were assiduous (shakedu) so that he would rejoice with her for three days, as it says later (Ketubot 5a). And [regarding] a virgin, where that reason does not apply — for one cannot say "he will rise early to his trade and go off," since she has seven days of feasting — therefore, because of blessing alone, they would not establish a [fixed] day.

Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:13:1.hebrew: אי איכא בתי דינין כו' - נראה לר"י, דמכל מקום אין נשאת בששי, דהא אין דנין בשבת. ועתה נוהגין לישא אף בששי, משום דאין ב"ד קבועין; ואם יש לו טענת בתולין, יכול לקבול בשבת בפני שלשה, כמו בשאר ימות השבוע. ועוד, לפירוש הקונטרס, דוקא בימיהם קבעו יום הנישואין, משום שעל ידי כך יתברר הדבר ויבואו עדים, מתוך שמתאספים העם לב"ד; ואין שייך לומר עכשיו כך:
Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:13:1.english: If there are courts, etc. - It appears to the Ri that nevertheless, [a virgin] is not married on Friday, for one does not judge on Shabbat. And now the custom is to marry even on Friday, because there are no established courts; and if he has a claim regarding virginity, he can lodge a complaint on Shabbat before three [men], just as on the other days of the week. And furthermore, according to the explanation of the Kunteres [Rashi], it was specifically in their days that they fixed the day of marriage, because through this the matter would be clarified and witnesses would come, since the people assemble at the court; and it is not applicable to say so now.

Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:1:1.hebrew: וסברה דאניס - ומן הדין לית לן למיחש דלמא אניס הוא, דרובן לא אניסי; ולהכי קרי להו צנועות, שמחמירים על עצמן, אע"ג דמצי לאינסובי. וגבי פרוצות לא גרסינן וסברה דלא אניס, אלא ואמרה דלא אניס; פי', אפילו כשיצא הקול דאניס אמרה דלא אניס, או אפילו כשתדע היא עצמה דאניס ואחרים לא ידעו. ואם תאמר: מת תוך י"ב חודש נמי יהא גט מהאי טעמא, דזימנין דלא מת וסברה דמת, ומיעגנא ויתבה? ויש לומר, דמיתה קלא אית לה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:1:1.english: And she thinks that he was prevented by an accident - And strictly speaking, we do not need to be concerned that perhaps he was prevented by an accident, for the majority [of people] are not prevented by accidents. And therefore [the Gemara] calls them "scrupulous women" (tzenu'ot), because they are stringent upon themselves even though they could [lawfully] remarry. And regarding licentious women (perutzot), our reading is not: "and she thinks that he was not prevented by an accident," but rather: "and she says that he was not prevented by an accident." Meaning: even when a rumor circulated that he was prevented by an accident, she says that he was not prevented by an accident; or even when she herself knows that he was prevented by an accident and others do not know. And if you say: [If he] died within twelve months, let it also be a [valid] get for this reason — for at times he did not die, but she thinks that he died, and she will remain bound and sit [unmarried]! And one can say that death generates a report (has publicity).

Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:3:1.english: [He] betroths with the consent of the Rabbis - Therefore, they say at the time of betrothal (kiddushin): "According to the law of Moses and Israel."

Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:3:2.english: And the Rabbis annulled the betrothal from her - At the beginning of [the chapter] HaSholeiach (Gittin 33a), I explained [this].

Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:4:1.hebrew: תינח דקדיש בכספא - דהפקר ב"ד היה הפקר, והוו מעות מתנה, וממילא יהו כל בעילותיו זנות. קדיש בביאה, מאי איכא למימר? איך יפקיעו ביאה של קידושין? ואפי' למ"ד בהאשה רבה (יבמות פט: ושם) דיש כח לחכמים לעקור דבר מן התורה, היינו כגון דליכא עבירה, כההיא דהאשה רבה דהדר לטיבלא; אבל היכא דאיכא עבירה, דמקודשת היא בביאה, מאי איכא למימר? ומשני: שויוה רבנן בעילותיו בעילת זנות, ואין כאן קדושין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:4:1.english: Granted if he betrothed with money - For [property declared] ownerless by the court is ownerless (hefker beit din haya hefker), and the money becomes a gift, and consequently all his cohabitations become [acts of] licentiousness (zenut). [If] he betrothed with intercourse, what can be said? How can they expropriate an act of intercourse of betrothal? And even according to the one who said in [the chapter of] "Ha'isha Rabbah" (Yevamot 89b and there) that the Sages have the power to uproot a matter from the Torah, that is [only] where there is no transgression, like that [case] in "Ha'isha Rabbah" where [the produce] reverts to untithed produce (tevel); but where there is a transgression, since she is betrothed with intercourse, what can be said? And [the Gemara] answers: The Rabbis rendered his cohabitations an act of licentiousness (zenut), and there is no betrothal here.

Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:5:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי אמר רבא וכן לענין גיטין - פסק ר"ח כלישנא קמא, דאין אונס בגיטין. והביא ראיה מדקאמר סתמא הש"ס בריש השולח (גיטין לד. ושם), גבי ההוא דאמר: "אי לא נסיבנא עד תלתין יומין ליהוי גיטא כו'", ואי משום אונס — אין אונס בגיטין. וכן נראה, דאליבא דאיכא דאמרי הוו פירכי מכל הני דמייתי סייעתא ללישנא קמא, ולא סמכינן אשינויי דחיקי. וקשה לר"י, דמסיק בפרק מי שאחזו (גיטין עג. ושם), דבין דאמר "הרי זה גיטיך אם מתי מחולי זה", בין אם אמר "אם לא אעמוד מחולי זה", ונפל עליו הבית או נשכו נחש או אכלו ארי — דלא הוי גט; אלמא דיש אונס בגיטין! וליכא למימר דהתם לא מטעם דיש אונס קאמר דלא הוי גט, אלא משום דבין אם מתי מחולי זה בין אם לא אעמוד משמע שימות מחמת זה החולי, וכשנפל עליו הבית או נשכו נחש אינו גט דאין זה מחולי זה — דהא מוכח בהדיא התם דמטעם דיש אונס הוא, גבי ההוא גברא דזבין ארעא לחבריה וקביל עליה כל אונסא דאיתיליד בה כו', אמר רבא: "אונס דלא שכיח הוא", ומייתי רבא סייעתא מהא דאכלו ארי אינו גט; אלמא אונס דלא שכיח יש טענת אונס לרבא! והכא קאמר רבא גופיה בלישנא קמא, שהוא עיקר, דאין אונס אפילו באונס דלא שכיח, כדמוכח הסוגיא! ואור"י, דג' ענייני אונס הן: דאונס דלא שכיח כלל, כההיא דמי שאחזו — אפי' ללישנא קמא דרבא דהכא יש אונס, דלא שייך התם לתקן משום צנועות ומשום פרוצות, דלעולם לא סברי צנועות דנפל עליו הבית או שהכישו נחש כיון דלא שכיח כלל, ומשום פרוצות נמי ליכא למיחש כיון דלא שכיח שיעשה כן; ואונס דשכיח, כגון ההיא דפסקיה מברא — אפילו לאיכא דאמרי אין אונס, דאיבעי ליה לאתנויי; אבל אונס דשכיח ולא שכיח — בהא פליגי תרי לישני דרבא. והלכתא כלישנא קמא דרבא, כדפירשנו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 3a:5:1.english: Some say: Rava said, And so too regarding bills of divorce - Rabbeinu Chananel ruled in accordance with the first version, that there is no [claim of] unavoidable accident in [the matter of] bills of divorce. And he brought proof from that which the anonymous [voice of] the Gemara says at the beginning of [the chapter] HaSholei'ach (Gittin 34a and ibid.), regarding that [man] who said: "If I do not marry [her] within thirty days, let [this] be a get, etc.," and [the Gemara asks]: And if [it is] on account of an unavoidable accident? There is no [claim of] unavoidable accident in bills of divorce! And so it appears [as well], for according to the "Some say" [version], all those [sources] that brought support for the first version would be refutations [against it], and we do not rely on forced resolutions. And the Ri raises a difficulty: For [the Gemara] concludes in the chapter Mi She'achazo (Gittin 73a and ibid.) that whether he said, "This is your get if I die from this illness," or whether he said, "if I do not recover from this illness," and the house collapsed on him, or a snake bit him, or a lion devoured him, that it is not a get. Consequently, [this indicates] that there is [a claim of] unavoidable accident in bills of divorce! And one cannot say that there, it is not on account of [the principle that] "there is [a claim of] unavoidable accident" that it says that it is not a get, but rather because whether [he said] "if I die from this illness" or "if I do not recover," it implies that he must die on account of this illness, and when the house collapsed on him or a snake bit him it is not a get because this is not from this illness — for it is explicitly proven there that it is on account of [the principle that] "there is [a claim of] unavoidable accident," regarding that man who sold land to his fellow and accepted upon himself [liability for] any accident that should occur to it, etc., [and] Rava said: "It is an uncommon accident," and Rava brings support from that [case where] "a lion devoured him, it is not a get." Evidently, [in the case of] an uncommon accident, there is a claim of unavoidable accident according to Rava! And here Rava himself says in the first version, which is primary, that there is no [claim of] unavoidable accident even in [the case of] an uncommon accident, as the sugya proves! And the Ri says that there are three categories of unavoidable accident: For an accident that is not common at all, like that [case in the chapter] Mi She'achazo, even according to the first version of Rava here, there is [a claim of] unavoidable accident, as it was not applicable there to institute an ordinance on account of modest women and on account of licentious women; for modest women would never assume that a house collapsed on him or that a snake bit him, since it is not common at all, and regarding licentious women there is also no reason to be concerned, since it is not common that this should happen. And a common accident, such as that [case where] the ferry was halted, even according to the "Some say" [version] there is no [claim of] unavoidable accident, for he should have stipulated. But an accident that is somewhat common and somewhat uncommon — regarding this, the two versions of Rava disagree. And the halakhah is in accordance with the first version of Rava, as we explained.
